## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The **Bhikṣuṇī-vibhaṅga of the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya** in twenty fascicles, presenting the 354-rule *bhikṣuṇī*-prātimokṣa with its *vibhaṅga* exposition. Translated by **Yìjìng** ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8)) at Cháng'ān in the early 8th century. 苾芻尼 *bìchúnī* is Yìjìng's preferred transliteration of *bhikṣuṇī*, replacing the older 比丘尼 *bǐqiūnī* — the change reflects Yìjìng's commitment to recovering the "correct" Sanskrit pronunciation of monastic terms.

**Abstract**

The Mūlasarvāstivāda *bhikṣuṇī-vibhaṅga* is one of the four extant complete *bhikṣuṇī-vibhaṅgas* in the Chinese canon (alongside the Mahīśāsaka [KR6k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0001) sec., Mahāsāṃghika [KR6k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0006) sec., Dharmaguptaka [KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009) sec., and Sarvāstivāda [KR6k0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0016) sec.). The Mūlasarvāstivāda recension is the longest and most narrative-rich of the four. Its *bhikṣuṇī*-discipline reflects the late-Indian Mūlasarvāstivāda institutional setting at Nālandā in the 7th century, and is the textual basis of the Tibetan *bhikṣuṇī*-Vinaya (which, however, was never in fact transmitted to Tibet as a living lineage — the Tibetan *bhikṣuṇī*-saṅgha was never established in pre-modern times).
